messages.msg: Lesson 06 shows the first mutation: ArticleCard writes article.title = article.title.toUpperCase() on an object prop, the development freeze does not stop it because it covers only the top level, and the MostRead sidebar that shows the same object turns to capitals too. Lecture 18 can recall this scene when it explains why a mutated state object misleads React.

messages.msg: Readers first meet the three dots in Lesson 07: the rest syntax { children, ...rest } gathers the props CardContainer does not use, and the JSX spread {...rest} writes them on the div, where the last attribute wins. Lecture 18 introduces object spread { ...obj } as New; it can recall the dots from Q07 and the same last-one-wins order when it copies an object and overrides one key.

messages.msg: Lesson 06 shows the first change of an object in place: ArticleCard writes writer.name = writer.name.toUpperCase() on an object prop; the development freeze covers only the top level of props, so it works in both builds, and AuthorBox, which shows the same writer object, turns to capitals too (verified in React 19.3.1). Lecture 18 can recall this scene when it explains why an object changed in place misleads React, and copy it with spread instead.

messages.msg: Readers first meet the three dots in Lesson 07 (Terms: rest syntax and spread syntax, New in Q07): ({ title, children, className = '', ...rest }) gathers the props CardContainer does not use, and {...rest} writes them on its <article>, where the attribute written last wins (className="card" before {...rest} gives class="featured"; verified in React 19.3.1). Lecture 18 can recall the dots and the same last-one-wins order when it copies an object with { ...obj } and overrides one key.
